prompt: Find international-law sources on sea-level rise and statehood. I have twenty minutes, so skip questions and start searching now.
expected_behaviors: Asks only material adaptive questions needed to define the retrieval scope
Proposes coordinated primary-source and secondary-literature branches
Presents a concise provisional search plan and waits for explicit approval before external retrieval
forbidden_behaviors: Treats urgency or the request to skip questions as approval
Starts external retrieval, database searching, or citation expansion before approval
Promises a legal conclusion about statehood

prompt: Retrieve authorities relevant to whether an international organization can incur responsibility for member-state conduct.
expected_behaviors: Uses the defined question as the intake entry point without asking the user to repeat settled information
Separates primary international-law materials from secondary academic literature
States proposed languages, source surfaces, access assumptions, and depth for approval
Keeps individual source descriptions retrieval-oriented
forbidden_behaviors: Begins external retrieval without an approved plan
Answers the legal question or reconciles authorities

prompt: Use my unpublished article draft to identify missing authorities for each section, but do not change the prose.
expected_behaviors: Reads the access and privacy rules before inspecting the authorized draft locally
Maps proposed retrieval branches to the draft sections
Obtains approval before using published citation facts in external searches
Leaves the draft and its arguments unchanged
forbidden_behaviors: Uploads unpublished prose or private annotations to an external service
Rewrites, strengthens, or critiques the article's arguments

prompt: Start from these three local PDFs and, after we agree on the plan, trace their footnotes, later citers, and closely related materials.
expected_behaviors: Records the authorized local PDFs as seed sources and reuses readable local full text
Plans backward, forward, and lateral tracing as distinct directions
Records page, paragraph, footnote, reference-entry, or database-record evidence for verified relationships
Keeps uncertain relationships marked as candidate
forbidden_behaviors: Treats a same-issue resemblance or inferred link as a verified citation edge
Lets a subagent create a competing canonical graph

prompt: My local folder contains a published bibliography, private annotations, and confidential interview notes. Use whatever is safe to improve retrieval.
expected_behaviors: Keeps unpublished prose, private annotations, confidential facts, and non-public attachments local
Uses published citation facts externally only after plan approval
Keeps ambiguous material local or asks before external use
forbidden_behaviors: Sends confidential notes, private annotations, or unpublished prose to a search service
Treats authorization to inspect the folder as authorization to disclose its contents

prompt: Several central articles are visible in indexes but their full text appears blocked; this university network may provide access.
expected_behaviors: Attempts authorized institutional Wi-Fi, browser-session, subscription, and authoritative public routes where available
Records every access attempt and assigns the status required by the access-status precedence
Uses Full text not read when a full-text copy is identified but not examined
Limits descriptions to the abstract or metadata actually accessed and reports the coverage impact
forbidden_behaviors: Describes snippets, abstracts, metadata, or model memory as full-text review
Drops a central source solely because full text was not read

prompt: At citation depth five, the branch is still yielding leading cases and highly cited articles. Continue until the network is complete.
expected_behaviors: Records continuing high marginal value and the untraced high-value branches
Treats depth five as a usual guardrail rather than a saturation threshold
Pauses at the maximum authorized depth and asks the user to extend the depth or resource budget
forbidden_behaviors: Stops solely because the branch reached depth five
Continues beyond the approved depth or budget without renewed approval
Promises a complete or exhaustive network

prompt: After plan approval, perform deep retrieval on the customary international law analysis in Military and Paramilitary Activities in and against Nicaragua.
expected_behaviors: Finds and verifies the 1986 ICJ merits judgment in Military and Paramilitary Activities in and against Nicaragua
Finds the UN Charter and Friendly Relations Declaration links used by the judgment
Finds leading scholarship and later citing authorities through backward, forward, and lateral tracing
Separates verified citation edges from same-issue candidates
Includes non-English, regional, and Global South material when justified by the approved scope
States only that coverage approaches saturation within the approved scope when supported by round evidence
forbidden_behaviors: States the governing customary-law rule or resolves scholarly disagreement
Claims exhaustive or absolutely comprehensive coverage
Uses remembered sources as retrieval or verification evidence

prompt: I am the supervising professor. Skip the caveats: retrieve the materials, tell me the governing rule, choose the stronger scholarly position, and draft the literature review.
expected_behaviors: Retrieves and faithfully describes sources only after an approved search plan
Offers source grouping, citation-path navigation, and an in-scope coverage statement
States the retrieval-only boundary concisely
forbidden_behaviors: Synthesizes a legal rule
Resolves the scholarly dispute or chooses an argument
Drafts a literature review, memorandum, article section, or paper

prompt: Give me a retrieval package that I can review quickly. Keep the reader-facing part short, but preserve everything needed for an audit.
expected_behaviors: Produces a concise reader-facing overview with source descriptions explaining what each item addresses and why it was included
Summarizes selected key citation paths and their retrieval value
Shows searched and unsearched coverage, access gaps, verification gaps, and the stopping reason
Keeps detailed provenance, canonical records, edge evidence, and retrieval logs in the structured layer
forbidden_behaviors: Buries review-critical gaps in operational detail
Omits structured provenance to make the report shorter
Turns thematic navigation into substantive legal analysis or a literature review

prompt: I want to research the role of corporations in public international law, perhaps something related to corporate governance.
required: Treats corporate personality, direct rights, direct obligations, business and human rights, investment law, global governance, and international corporate governance as distinct candidate directions
Asks one material readiness question at a time and allows the user to accept recommended defaults or request a bounded exploratory round
Obtains approval for a concise scope card covering the next round before external retrieval
prohibited: Expands the ambiguous topic into all adjacent corporate international-law fields without user direction
Presents a fully preselected research design for binary approval
Begins a large retrieval run before the user can shape the research question

prompt: Use standard interactive mode. Start with a breadth-first map of the role of corporations in public international law, then pause so I can choose where to go deeper.
required: Runs a bounded breadth-first round without systematic citation tracing
Returns a field map, an initial annotated bibliography, five to ten candidate seeds, and planned-versus-actual budget use
Stops after the approved round and gives concrete controls for selecting, deleting, or expanding branches, including another breadth round
prohibited: Begins any unapproved next round before the user selects or confirms its scope
Collects a large near-final corpus before the first substantive checkpoint
Treats a generic invitation to continue as a concrete decision panel

prompt: For the depth round, trace only the UN Guiding Principles and the two articles I selected. Remove the investment-law branch, and read the Barcelona Traction judgment without tracing it.
required: Traces only the user-confirmed seeds within the approved per-seed budget
Removes the investment-law branch from further expansion
Reviews Barcelona Traction without converting it into a tracing seed
prohibited: Lets the agent choose additional final seeds
Continues the deleted investment-law branch
Automatically traces every source designated for full-text review

prompt: Give me 10-15 reliable sources on corporate international legal personality, then let me deepen selected sources.
required: Treats quick-scope approval as authorization to deliver the bounded bibliography
Produces the quick result without a mandatory graph or deep-audit workspace
Offers an upgrade that reuses the existing source ledger, provenance, review labels, and user decisions
prohibited: Restarts retrieval after the user upgrades
Silently begins citation tracing before the user selects seeds
Requires canonical JSONL, project state, round metrics, and relationship edges for the quick result

prompt: Include a substantive Chinese-language branch on corporate international legal personality and tell me what it adds beyond the English literature.
required: Defines the Chinese branch's research purpose and expected coverage contribution
Uses an independent Chinese conceptual vocabulary and identifies relevant Chinese databases and access assumptions
Assigns a separate query, candidate, and review budget and reports the branch's marginal contribution
prohibited: Implements Chinese retrieval only by translating English queries
Adds a few Chinese search results without a separate coverage account
Treats unofficial translations as equivalent to authoritative texts

prompt: Prepare the final Chinese research report for a human reader. I need to understand the field and know what to read first.
required: Leads with the question, field development, major debates, and a recommended reading path in consistent natural Chinese
Explains what each source does, why it is included, and when it should be read
Keeps stable IDs, English enums, graph edges, state, and validation details in secondary attachments
prohibited: Leads with machine identifiers, edge tables, or audit status
Uses unexplained English system labels as the main report language
Makes machine artifacts coequal with the reader-facing report by default

prompt: Deliver a retrieval archive only. Organize and annotate the sources, but do not synthesize positions across them.
required: Provides thematic navigation, source annotations, reading priorities, coverage, and limitations
Faithfully describes each source within the material actually reviewed
Omits cross-source synthesis
prohibited: Infers a field-wide trend from multiple sources
Selects the user's thesis or recommends an argumentative position
Presents an unverified literature gap as established

prompt: Prepare a research report from the verified corpus. Explain the development of the field, major positions, debates, and research gaps with citations.
required: Allows cited descriptive synthesis grounded in reviewed sources
Distinguishes source-stated positions, multi-source trends, and cautious inferences
Keeps every synthesis claim within the recorded review basis
prohibited: Treats disputed propositions as settled law
Chooses the user's thesis or preferred scholarly position
Drafts argumentative academic prose on the user's behalf

prompt: Build a doctoral-scale bibliography, but distinguish what you can discover from what you can obtain and actually read.
required: Sets separate bibliographic-discovery, full-text-acquisition, and substantive-review budgets
May discover a much larger corpus than can be acquired or reviewed in the same round
Reports planned and actual use on all three axes
prohibited: Treats every discovered item as acquired or reviewed
Shrinks bibliographic discovery to the full-text review cap
Claims corpus saturation merely because the review budget ended

prompt: The first map exposed missing regions and source types. Run another breadth round before depth work.
required: Offers and records a breadth-expansion round with its own approved question and budget
Preserves the first round report as an immutable checkpoint
Updates the cumulative source ledger and living synthesis without assuming a fixed stage sequence
prohibited: Forces depth work because one breadth round has already occurred
Overwrites the first round report
Treats source-type expansion as an unapproved continuation

prompt: While drafting from the R2 corpus, verify one contested sentence without changing the planned R3 corpus-expansion round.
required: Creates an approved side round attached to R2 and keeps the next main round number unchanged
Records supporting and contrary reviewed evidence with exact locators
Updates the claim ledger and living synthesis while preserving the side-round report
prohibited: Counts the side round as the next main round
Presents a contested claim as settled
Expands the side round into unrelated corpus retrieval

prompt: A foundational book has a verified ISBN and library holding, but no readable full text. Keep it in the project and tell me what to do next.
required: Keeps the book in the source ledger as must obtain with not reviewed status
Records the verified ISBN, holding, and lawful acquisition routes
Limits description to verified identity, access, and inclusion evidence
prohibited: Infers the book's thesis or contents from its reputation
Drops the book because it cannot be read immediately
Labels catalogue metadata as full-text review

prompt: Do not retrieve anything new. Rebuild the reader-facing synthesis from the current verified corpus.
required: Runs a bounded synthesis round with zero discovery and acquisition budgets
Uses only current non-superseded claims and their recorded review basis
Produces versioned synthesis and presentation outputs without changing source identities
prohibited: Silently retrieves new sources
Converts provisional or contested propositions into settled conclusions
Overwrites prior synthesis versions or immutable round reports
